security_privacy_cost_impact: A new write path: an owner, after step-up, can move their own active workspace to closing and back, through a SECURITY DEFINER command owned by app_command, audited in the same transaction; a refused audit write aborts the action. app_command gains its first grants (USAGE on app; SELECT (id, lifecycle_state) and UPDATE (lifecycle_state, updated_by) on app.workspaces; INSERT on app.audit_logs; EXECUTE on four app_authz helpers), each pinned. app_authz gains five column reads of workspace_member_scopes and an own-rows policy. The actor is bound to request.jwt.claims (RFC-2026-023 §4 and RFC-2026-026 §3.3/1's residual: a session that sets the claims and can execute a command writes as anyone it names; EXECUTE on the commands is authenticated's alone). Refusals about a workspace the actor is not an active member of are unrecorded (Q-026-10 (iii)). No secret, no PII, no network, no cost.
migration_and_data_impact: One forward migration, 172_acting_user_and_closing_command.sql; no table, column or data change. Four earlier apply-time blocks superseded with additive final-state replacements. The snapshot declares 172 not applied. No open_blockers line moves (the manifest's amendment list keeps four paths; [200] is added at the end).
